summary: Describes using the Stac LZS data compression algorithm, with one or several compression histories, to compress PPP packets. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: Stac LZS is a way to shrink the packets sent over a PPP link, by replacing repeated text with a short reference to earlier text. The two ends keep a shared memory of what has been sent, so a reference only makes sense if both ends have the same memory. This memo describes the packet formats and the rules that keep the two ends in step.

questions: what is ppp stac lzs compression
how does stac lzs work with ppp
what is a ppp compression history
subtitle: How Stac LZS compresses PPP packets, and how the two ends stay in step when a packet goes missing.

tldr.problem: A point-to-point link often carries the same data twice, and a long-lived compression history can only be used if both ends stay in step.
tldr.mechanism: Stac LZS compresses each PPP packet against a sliding window of earlier data, and keeps a separate history for each logical connection when more than one is negotiated. Sequence numbers, a check byte or a CRC detect a packet that was lost or corrupted.
tldr.outcome: When a mismatch is found the receiver asks for that history to be reset, and the sender clears it and confirms. The cost is that a mismatch costs the history, and compression can expand a packet by up to 12.5%.

facts.label: PPP protocol for a Stac LZS datagram

today: RFC 1974 is an Informational memo from August 1996, and the metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It describes the Stac LZS algorithm and the licence terms Stac Electronics offered for it, and its own security considerations section says only that security issues are not discussed in the memo.

sections.title: Introduction and Licensing
sections.content:
The Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) provides a standard method for transporting multi-protocol datagrams over point-to-point links, and the PPP Compression Control Protocol (CCP) provides a method to negotiate and use compression protocols over PPP encapsulated links. This memo describes the use of the Stac LZS data compression algorithm, with single or multiple compression histories, for compressing PPP encapsulated packets.

Starting from a sliding window compression history similar to LZ1, Stac Electronics developed the enhanced algorithm known as Stac LZS. The algorithm is optimized to compress all file types as efficiently as possible, and even string matches as short as two octets are effectively compressed. It supports both single compression history communication and multiple compression history communication. A single history needs the least memory to implement, but may not compress as well as a multiple history implementation. Multiple histories help when many streams of information are interleaved over the same link: each virtual link transmits data that is independent of the others, so associating a separate compression history with each virtual link can improve the compression ratio of the link.

Source and object licenses for the algorithm are available on a non-discriminatory basis, and hardware implementations are also available. The memo also states the meaning of the requirement words it uses: MUST and MUST NOT mark absolute requirements and absolute prohibitions, SHOULD marks an item that may be ignored for good reason if the implications are understood, and MAY marks one of a set of allowed alternatives.
sections.plainLanguage: Compression works by replacing text that has already been sent with a short pointer back to it. The pointer only makes sense if both ends have kept the same record of what was sent, and that record is called the compression history.

sections.title: LZS Packets on a PPP Link
sections.content:
Before any LZS packets may be communicated, PPP must reach the Network-Layer Protocol phase. When the Compression Control Protocol has reached the Opened state and LZS is negotiated as the primary compression algorithm, exactly one Stac LZS datagram is encapsulated in the PPP Information field, and the PPP Protocol field indicates type hex 00FD, compressed datagram, or type hex 00FB, individual link compressed datagram. Type 00FD is used when compression is negotiated over a single physical link, or over a single bundle consisting of multiple physical links. Type 00FB is used when compression is negotiated separately over individual physical links to the same destination.

When CCP has not successfully reached the Opened state, or LZS is not the primary compression algorithm, exactly one LZS datagram is still encapsulated in the PPP Information field, but the PPP Protocol field indicates type hex 4021, Stac LZS. In that case use of LZS is terminated by the PPP LCP Protocol-Reject, and the default format is used: a single history with no History Number field and no Check Value field, as if the negotiated history count were 1.

The maximum length of the Stac LZS datagram transmitted over a PPP link is the same as the maximum length of the Information field of a PPP encapsulated packet. Before compression, the uncompressed data begins with the PPP Protocol ID Field, and Protocol-Field-Compression may be used on that value if it has been successfully negotiated for the link. The PPP Protocol ID Field is followed by the original Information field. PPP Link Control Protocol packets must not be sent within Stac LZS packets, and neither must PPP Network Control Protocol packets.

Padding and zero handling are also specified. The LZS Information field always ends with the last compressed data byte, the end marker, which is used to disambiguate padding, so trailing bits as well as whole octets can be treated as padding. When the sender does not add padding, any trailing zero octets may be removed before transmission, and a single trailing zero octet must be appended upon receipt, after the removal of any framing FCS.
sections.plainLanguage: Once compression is agreed, each packet carries a marker in the PPP protocol field saying that its contents are compressed. The compressed data itself ends with a marker byte, so the receiver can tell where the data stops and the padding starts.

sections.title: Packet Format, History Number and Check Value
sections.content:
The Stac LZS packet holds a 2 octet PPP Protocol field, then an optional History Number field and an optional Check Value field, then the compressed data. The PPP Protocol field is 00FD or 00FB once the protocol has been negotiated, and that value may itself be compressed when Protocol-Field-Compression is negotiated.

The History Number field comprises 0, 1 or 2 octets and names the compression history that was used, ranging from 2 to the negotiated History Count. By default a History Count of 1 is supported and the field is not present, because there is no need for it when no history is kept or only a single history is kept. If the negotiated History Count is 2 or more but less than 256, the field is 1 octet. If 256 or more histories are negotiated, the field is 2 octets, most significant octet first.

The Check Value field also comprises 0, 1 or 2 octets, and by default a sequence number check is added to the packet, which is 1 octet. Three check methods are defined. A one octet Longitudinal Check Byte (LCB) may be used after successful negotiation of the LCB option: it is the exclusive-OR of FF and each octet of the uncompressed datagram before compression, and the receiver computes the same value over the decompressed packet and compares it with the received one. A two octet Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) may be used instead of the LCB, after successful negotiation of the CRC option. The transmitter initializes the CRC to FFFF at the beginning of each packet, the computation is based on the HDLC FCS-16 polynomial x16 + x12 + x5 + 1, and the ones complement of the CRC is transmitted least significant octet first. A one octet Sequence Number may be used instead of the LCB or CRC: after CCP has reached the open state the transmitter sets the sequence number to 1 and increments it modulo 256 on successive packets that contain data fields, relative to the history number used, and the receiver keeps an internal reference value of the next expected sequence number for each history, starting at 1. A received packet whose sequence number does not match that reference has caused a receive failure, and it is silently discarded.

The compressed data field must contain only one datagram in compressed form, its length is always a whole number of octets, and there must be exactly one end marker per block of compressed data. The form of the data field is one block of compressed data as defined in section 3.2 of X3.241-1994, repeated in the memo for information only: a compressed stream is an optional compressed string followed by an end marker, a compressed string is either a raw byte or a compressed run given by an offset and a length, the offset is 7 or 11 bits, the end marker is 110000000, and the length code runs from 2 to 24 bytes.
sections.plainLanguage: Each compressed packet says which history it used and carries a check on the data. Three kinds of check are on offer: a one byte sum, a two byte CRC, and a one byte counter that shows whether any packet has gone missing.

sections.title: Sending Packets and Recovering the Histories
sections.content:
The transmitter assigns each network datagram to a particular history buffer and processes it to form compressed data. If a Reset-Request is outstanding for the buffer to be used, or if the negotiated history count for the data link is 0, the buffer is cleared before the compression. Uncompressed data must be sent, in the original PPP packet form with the native PPP Protocol ID number, when compression causes enough expansion to exceed the Information field's maximum receive unit. Because the compressor has already modified the history buffer in that case, the buffer must be cleared before the next datagram is processed. On receipt of a CCP Reset-Request, the transmitting compressor is cleared to an initial state, which includes clearing the history buffer, and a CCP Reset-Ack is transmitted with the two octet history number in its data field.

The receiver signals its compression engine when a Reset-Request arrives, and clears any outstanding receive failure when a Reset-Ack arrives. If no receive failure is outstanding and the sequence number field is present, its value is checked. If no failure is detected, the data is assigned to the indicated decompression history buffer and decompressed, and any LCB or CRC present on the received datagram is computed over the uncompressed data and checked against the received value. Any failure is handled by the history resynchronization mechanism.

The History Count field determines the number of history buffers maintained for the compression protocol, and each buffer could represent a separate logical connection between the compression peers. While a history is maintained, the peers must use link error detection and signalling so that the compressor and decompressor copies of each buffer stay identical. A History Count of 0 means compression on a connectionless basis: a single history buffer is used and must be cleared at the beginning of every datagram. A count of 1 means a single buffer is maintained by each peer, one logical connection. A count greater than 1 means separate history buffers, error detection states and signalling states are kept for each history, and the compressing peer may transmit data on any number of them, up to the negotiated count.

Recovery uses the CCP Reset-Request and Reset-Ack mechanism, which allows a receiver failure in one direction to be signalled without affecting traffic in the other direction. Reset-Requests and Reset-Acks are specific to the history number of the packet that carries them, and a receive failure is determined by the LCB, the CRC or the sequence number according to the check mode. As with all compression algorithms, the decompressor cannot recover from dropped, erroneous or mis-ordered datagrams, and will propagate errors until both peers are reset to an initial state. The protocol therefore provides both the detection, through the LCB or CRC for erroneous datagrams and the sequence number for dropped or mis-ordered ones, and the correction, by clearing the failing compression and decompression histories and following the transmitter and receiver processes again.
sections.plainLanguage: If a packet is lost, the two ends no longer agree on what has been sent, and every later packet would be wrong. So the receiver notices, asks for that one history to be thrown away, and the two ends start that history again from empty.

sections.title: The Configuration Option
sections.content:
The CCP Stac LZS Configuration Option negotiates the use of Stac LZS on the link. By ultimate disagreement, no compression is used, and all implementations must support the default values. The option carries a Type of 17 and a Length of 5, followed by a two octet History Count field and a one octet Check Mode field.

The History Count field is two octets, most significant octet first, and specifies the maximum number of compression histories. A value of 0 means the implementation expects the peer to clear the compression history at the beginning of every packet. A value of 1 is the default and means that only one history is maintained. Other valid values range from 2 to 65535. The peer is not required to send as many histories as the implementation says it can accept, but resources are allocated in each peer to support the number of histories negotiated in this field.

The Check Mode field indicates support for LCB, CRC or sequence number checking, and other future extensions to the standard. It comprises 2 sub-fields and is bit-mapped: the 3 least significant bits hold 5 mutually exclusive values, and the upper 5 bits are reserved bit locations that must be set to 0 so that future backward-compatible extensions are possible. For compatibility, sequence numbers must be implemented and the other four check modes may be. The defined values are 0 for None, which may be implemented but requires a history count of zero, 1 for LCB, 2 for CRC, 3 for Sequence Number and 4 for Extended Mode.
sections.plainLanguage: The two ends agree two things before compressing: how many separate histories to keep, and how to check each packet. Every implementation must support the counter, because it is what detects a lost packet.

sections.title: Extended Mode
sections.content:
When Check Mode 4, Extended Mode, is successfully negotiated, the packet format differs from the format described earlier. Extended Mode supports only a history count of 1. The header holds the PPP Protocol field, four flag bits and a 12 bit Coherency Count, followed by the compressed data. Protocol-Field-Compression must not be used on the protocol value when Extended Mode is negotiated, even if it was negotiated earlier, and zero deletion and insertion must not be performed.

Bit A, PACKET_FLUSHED, says the history buffer has just been reset before this packet was generated, so the packet can always be decompressed because it is not based on any previous history. It is typically sent to tell the peer that it has reset its history buffer and that the peer can accept the packet and re-synchronize. Bit B is not used with Stac LZS compression. Bit C, PACKET_COMPRESSED, says whether the packet is compressed, with a value of 0 for uncompressed data and 1 for compressed data. Bit D is not used.

The coherency count is used to assure that packets are sent in proper order and that no packet has been dropped. It is initialized to the value 0x000, is always increased by 1 after each PPP packet is sent, and returns to 0 when all bits are 1. It is 12 bits, so the decompressor must handle the rollover case. When the compressor's history is cleared, for instance because a Reset-Request was received, the PACKET_FLUSHED bit must be set in the header of the next transmitted data packet, and if the compression caused the packet to expand then the packet is sent uncompressed with Bit A set and Bit C clear.

Synchronization in Extended Mode needs no Reset-Ack packet. If the decompressor's coherency count does not match the one in the received packet, or if it detects that a received packet is corrupted, it drops the packet and sends a CCP Reset-Request. The compressor, on receiving that packet, resets the history buffer and sets the PACKET_FLUSHED bit in the next frame it sends. The decompressor, on receiving a packet with the PACKET_FLUSHED bit set, resets its history buffer and sets its coherency count to the one the compressor shipped in that packet.
sections.plainLanguage: Extended Mode replaces the counter and the reset handshake with a single 12 bit count in the packet header. When the count does not line up, the receiver throws the packet away and asks for a reset, and the sender marks its next packet so the receiver knows to start again.

viz.caption: THE STAC LZS PACKET FORMAT FROM RFC 1974

items.label: None
items.desc: May be implemented, but then the history count must be zero.

items.label: LCB
items.desc: One octet longitudinal check byte over the uncompressed datagram.

items.label: CRC
items.desc: Two octet cyclic redundancy check using the HDLC FCS-16 polynomial.

items.label: Sequence Number
items.desc: One octet counter per history. This one must be implemented.

items.label: Extended Mode
items.desc: A different packet format with a 12 bit coherency count.

viz.caption: HISTORY MODES AND THE MESSAGES THAT RESET THEM

items.title: History Count 0
items.text: Compression is connectionless. One buffer, cleared at the start of every datagram.

items.title: History Count 1
items.text: The default. One buffer kept between packets, which is one logical connection.

items.title: History Count 2 to 65535
items.text: Separate buffers, error states and signalling states for each history.

items.title: Reset-Request
items.text: Code 14. Sent when a receive failure is detected, naming the history to reset.

items.title: Reset-Ack
items.text: Code 15. The peer confirms it has cleared that history. The data field holds the history number.

items.title: Uncompressed fallback
items.text: If compression expands the packet past the peer's maximum receive unit, send it in the original PPP form and clear the history.
